metadata.summary: Jacob Fearnley retired with an injury after losing 5-1 in the first set against Arthur Fery to give his fellow countryman a place in the second round at the Vienna Open.

Fearnley was broken by Fery in just his second service game, with the British No 1 winning the next two games on the bounce and looking set to consign his opponent to a comprehensive first-set loss. Fearnley, though, then put a stop to the contest, shaking the umpire's hand and retiring with an unspecified injury, allowing Fery safe passage to the next stage of the competition. England captain and Bayern Munich striker Kane is the bookmakers' favourite to become the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001. Victory would see Kane become just the fifth English winner of the Ballon d'Or after Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Owen, while he would also become the first Bayern player to claim it in 45 years. messages.text: Smith beats Schindler in Dortmund thriller after Littler's QF exit

metadata.summary: Ross Smith has won the Machineseeker European Championship for a second time after overcoming a late Martin Schindler fightback to claim an 11-8 victory in Dortmund.
metadata.content: European Championship Darts: Ross Smith beats Martin Schindler to Dortmund title after Luke Littler's quarter-final exit | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content European Championship Darts: Ross Smith beats Martin Schindler to Dortmund title after Luke Littler's quarter-final exit Luke Littler suffered a quarter-final exit to Krzysztof Ratajski, extending his wait for his elusive ranked TV title; Ross Smith beat Martin Schindler in the European Championship final; Watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports from November 14-22 Ali Stafford Senior Sports Journalist Sunday 25 October 2026 23:26, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the winning moment from Ross Smith's European Championship success, where he closed out an 11-8 victory over Martin Schindler. (Credit: ITV) Ross Smith has won the Machineseeker European Championship for a second time after overcoming a late Martin Schindler fightback to claim an 11-8 victory in Dortmund. The 2022 champion fired a 107 average in his last-eight victory over Luke Woodhouse and rallied from 4-1 down to beat Gerwyn Price 11-7, setting up a showdown against German No 1 Schindler at Westfalenhallen. Smith edged a tight opening session before reeling off six straight legs against Schindler, who almost fell 9-2 behind before capitalising on some wayward finishing to sneak a 20-dart break of throw. messages.text: 'Quality of drivers very low' - Alonso criticises Albon after clash

metadata.summary: Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso hit out at Williams' Alex Albon and stated the quality of drivers in the bottom third of the grid is "very low" after the pair collided at the United States Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Fernando Alonso criticises Alex Albon and says 'quality of drivers is very low' in bottom third of F1 field at United States GP | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Fernando Alonso criticises Alex Albon and says 'quality of drivers is very low' in bottom third of F1 field at United States GP Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso and Williams' Alex Albon collided on the opening lap of the United States Grand Prix; Alonso criticised Albon and hit out at other drivers in the midfield; watch every session of the Mexico City GP from Friday, live on Sky Sports F1 Monday 26 October 2026 08:54, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fernando Alonso has criticised 'low quality bottom third drivers' following his collision with Alex Albon. Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso hit out at Williams' Alex Albon and stated the quality of drivers in the bottom third of the grid is "very low" after the pair collided at the United States Grand Prix. Albon tried to overtake Alonso for 12th place into the Turn 11 hairpin on the opening lap, but went into the side of the Aston Martin driver, damaging both cars. Neither driver received a penalty and both were able to continue with Alonso finishing 16th and Albon in 17th in Austin.
